rows: Compliance with WoAG Protective Security Directions
The Accountable Authority complies with all Protective Security Directions.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority complies with all Protective Security Directions issued under the Protective Security Policy Framework.
Ensure the NDIA Accountable Authority complies with all whole-of-government Protective Security Directions to maintain WoAG security standards.
Non-compliance with PSPF Directions; regulatory breach; reputational and legal risk to the NDIA
Review all PSPF Directions upon publication and incorporate into the NDIA security governance framework. Report compliance status in the annual protective security report.

1. Monitor PSPF Directions published by Department of Home Affairs. 2. Brief Accountable Authority on new Directions. 3. Update NDIA security policies to reflect Directions. 4. Report compliance in annual report.

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Accountable Authority Ministerial Accountability for Protective Security
The Accountable Authority is answerable to their minister for the entity's protective security.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority is answerable to the responsible Minister for the entity's protective security posture and performance.
Establish clear lines of ministerial accountability for the NDIA's protective security, ensuring executive responsibility is transparent and enforced.
Unclear accountability for security failures; breakdown in governance and ministerial oversight
Accountable Authority (CEO); NDIA Executive Leadership Team
Establish formal reporting lines from Accountable Authority to Minister covering protective security matters. Include security performance in ministerial briefings and reporting cycles.

1. Document accountability arrangements in security governance framework. 2. Brief Minister on significant security events as required. 3. Include protective security in annual ministerial reporting. 4. Maintain records of ministerial briefings.
NDIA Board; NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Accountable Authority Responsibility for Security Risk Management
The Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of their entity.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of the entity.
Ensure ultimate responsibility for NDIA security risk management rests with the Accountable Authority, creating accountability at the highest level.
Unmanaged security risks; failure to identify and treat entity-level threats; inadequate risk governance
Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA operations and systems

The Accountable Authority must formally own the NDIA's security risk register, approve the risk tolerance, and receive regular risk reporting. Risk management must be embedded in corporate governance processes.

1. Maintain enterprise security risk register. 2. Report risk status to Accountable Authority at least quarterly. 3. Obtain formal AA approval for risk tolerance and treatment decisions. 4. Include risk status in annual report.
Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Chief Risk Officer
General Counsel; Audit Committee; NDIA Board
NDIA Executive Leadership Team; Department of Home Affairs

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
A Chief Security Officer is appointed and empowered to oversee the entity's protective security arrangements.
The NDIA shall appoint and empower a Chief Security Officer to oversee the entity's protective security arrangements.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2
Ensure a suitably qualified and empowered security executive is responsible for all protective security arrangements across the NDIA.
Absence of dedicated security leadership; uncoordinated protective security arrangements; gaps in security governance

Formally appoint a CSO with a documented mandate, appropriate delegation, and direct access to the Accountable Authority. CSO must have authority to direct security activities across all NDIA business lines.

1. Establish CSO position and position description. 2. Issue formal instrument of appointment. 3. Document delegations and authorities. 4. Ensure CSO has direct reporting line to Accountable Authority.
General Counsel; People and Culture; NDIA Security Team
All NDIA Branch Managers; Department of Home Affairs

The CSO must be empowered with sufficient authority and resources to fulfil their mandate. The PSPF requires the CSO to be a separate role from the CISO.
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
CSO Seniority and Minimum Security Clearance
The Chief Security Officer is a Senior Executive Service officer and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Security Officer is a Senior Executive Service officer and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3, A.7.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PS-3
Ensure the CSO has the requisite seniority, authority and trustworthiness to perform the role and access sensitive protective security information.
CSO lacking authority or clearance to access classified information; compromised security governance at executive level
Verify CSO position is classified at SES Band 1 or above. Initiate and maintain a minimum NV1 security clearance through AGSVA. Monitor clearance status and initiate renewal prior to expiry.
1. Confirm CSO position is at SES level. 2. Submit clearance request to AGSVA if NV1 not held. 3. Monitor clearance expiry dates. 4. Record clearance status in personnel security register.
Chief Security Officer (CSO); People and Culture; NDIA Security Vetting Team
NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
The Chief Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for protective security matters.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for all protective security matters.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2
Establish a clear and direct accountability relationship between the CSO and Accountable Authority to ensure security matters receive appropriate executive attention.
Protective security outcomes not escalated appropriately; lack of executive-level accountability for security failures
Formalise the CSO's accountability through documented reporting lines and governance structures. CSO must have regular direct access to the Accountable Authority to report on security matters.

1. Document CSO reporting line to Accountable Authority in governance framework. 2. Schedule regular security briefings (at minimum quarterly). 3. CSO to present at Audit Committee meetings. 4. Record meetings and outcomes.

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Appointment of Chief Information Security Officer
A Chief Information Security Officer is appointed to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security for the entity's most critical technology resources.
The NDIA shall appoint a Chief Information Security Officer to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security of its most critical technology resources.

Ensure a dedicated executive is responsible for the NDIA's cyber security program, providing leadership and oversight of cyber security across all critical technology assets.

All NDIA technology systems and data; Accountable Authority

Formally appoint a CISO with a documented mandate covering the cyber security program and critical technology resources. The CISO role should be separate from the CSO. Ensure the CISO has authority to direct cyber security activities across all technology systems.

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Security Practitioner Capability, Empowerment and Resourcing
Where appointed, security practitioners are appropriately skilled, empowered and resourced to perform their designated functions.
The NDIA shall ensure that, where appointed, security practitioners are appropriately skilled, empowered and resourced to perform their designated security functions.
Ensure security practitioners across the NDIA have the skills, authority and resources necessary to perform their security functions effectively.
Security practitioners unable to perform duties effectively; skill gaps leading to inadequate security controls; under-resourced security functions
All designated security practitioners across the NDIA
Personnel not in designated security practitioner roles

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Security Practitioner Access to Government Training
Where appointed, security practitioners have access to training across government to maintain and upskill on new and emerging security issues.
The NDIA shall ensure that, where appointed, security practitioners have access to government security training to maintain and upskill on new and emerging security issues.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 7.2, A.6.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AT-3

All designated security practitioners across the NDIA
Personnel not in designated security practitioner roles

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Accountable Authority Approval of Security Governance Arrangements
The Accountable Authority approves security governance arrangements that are tailored to the entity's size, complexity and risk environment.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority approves security governance arrangements tailored to the entity's size, complexity and risk environment.
Ensure the NDIA's security governance arrangements are formally approved by the Accountable Authority and are proportionate to the NDIA's size, risk profile and operational complexity.

All NDIA security governance structures and committees; Accountable Authority

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Dedicated Security Communication Channel (Security Email Address)
A dedicated security email address is established and monitored as the central conduit for distribution of protective security-related information across the entity.
The NDIA shall establish and maintain a dedicated security email address as the central conduit for distributing protective security-related information across the entity.
Ensure a monitored, centralised communication channel exists for distributing protective security information to all relevant NDIA personnel promptly and reliably.
Delayed or missed distribution of security information; communication gaps during security incidents; personnel unaware of security advisories
All NDIA personnel; NDIA Security Team

Create and maintain a dedicated security email address (e.g., security@ndia.gov.au). Ensure the mailbox is monitored during business hours and that a process exists for urgent after-hours matters. Distribute all PSPF-related communications, security advisories and incident notifications through this channel.
Email system configuration; access controls and monitoring for security mailbox; distribution list management

1. Provision dedicated security mailbox in NDIA email system. 2. Assign monitoring responsibilities to security team. 3. Establish distribution lists for different security communication types. 4. Test mailbox operability regularly.

All NDIA staff; Department of Home Affairs

Annual Cyber Security Survey Submission to ASD
The annual Cyber Security Survey is submitted to the Australian Signals Directorate.

The NDIA shall complete and submit the annual Cyber Security Survey to the Australian Signals Directorate in accordance with PSPF Requirement 35, ensuring the survey accurately reflects the NDIA's cyber security maturity and posture, supported by documented evidence.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 9.1, 9.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-7, PM-6; ASD Essential Eight Maturity Model

Ensure the NDIA participates in whole-of-government cyber security performance reporting by submitting an accurate and timely annual Cyber Security Survey to ASD, demonstrating the Agency's cyber security maturity and commitment to continuous improvement.

Failure to submit the annual Cyber Security Survey; inaccurate or unsubstantiated survey responses; non-compliance with PSPF Req 35; inability to demonstrate cyber security maturity to ASD; gaps in whole-of-government cyber security visibility.
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); NDIA Cyber Security team; all NDIA ICT systems and technology assets assessed against the Essential Eight and other ASD survey metrics.

Duty to Govern the Commonwealth Entity
